symptom: In `change $Order … on error without rollback begin … end error; set $N = $N + 10; commit $Order on error …`, the change's handler rejoined at the commit handler's merge AFTER the commit, so at runtime an error in the change skipped the set and the commit. check, exec and mx check reported nothing; describe showed one shared `join rejoin1`.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go addChangeObjectAction / addChangeVariableAction / addReplaceListAction pass no skip variable to finishCustomErrorHandler. Test: mdl/executor/error_handler_rejoin_change_2421_test.go
cause: finishCustomErrorHandler's skip variable defers a handler's rejoin until no later statement references it — right for an activity that CREATES the variable (it does not exist on the error path), but change/set/replace passed the variable they MODIFY, which exists on both paths, so every later use of $Order pushed the rejoin further down.
insight: **A 'skip' variable must be one the activity produces, not one it touches.** The skip exists so a handler does not rejoin before statements that need an object the failed activity never made; passing a pre-existing variable turns that into 'skip every later statement that mentions it'. Measured on 11.12.6: ChangeSetCommit and a three-change chain each rejoin right after their own activity; mx check 0 errors. `create` keeps the skip (control test).
